{"id": "2971e022-3d10-407d-88d1-f709b36d0430", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_a0ABT631bmtRKtyCzhJIwE", "content": "[{'text': '# Finish-Reason Drift Analysis\\n\\n**A small check with outsized value.** The finish-reason distribution is an early,\\notherwise-invisible indicator of quality regression that **no AWS alarm watches by default**. It\\ncosts almost nothing to monitor and it moves *before* users file complaints \u2014 which is exactly why\\nthe OpsAI strategy calls it out as a first-class quality signal rather than a footnote.\\n\\nThis reference backs two checks:\\n\\n- **LLM-EVAL-012** \u2014 the finish-reason distribution *shift itself* (the regression signal).\\n- **LLM-EVAL-013** \u2014 the *metric filter being absent*, so the shift can never be seen. This is the\\n  in-skill id for an absent `stopReason` metric filter.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Why the finish-reason distribution is a quality signal\\n\\nEvery Bedrock invocation ends for a reason, recorded in the `stopReason` field of the invocation\\nlog. Over a healthy, stable workload the mix of those reasons is roughly constant. When the mix\\n*moves* \u2014 specifically when more and more responses end in `max_tokens` (truncation) instead of\\n`end_turn` (natural completion) \u2014 the model is increasingly being cut off mid-answer. Truncated\\nanswers read as lower quality to users (dropped conclusions, half-finished code, missing final\\nsteps), but nothing in the default `AWS/Bedrock` metric set surfaces it. Latency looks fine; error\\nrates look fine; invocation counts look fine. The only visible symptom is a slow drift in a\\ndistribution nobody is trending.\\n\\nBecause the shift **precedes visible quality complaints by hours or days**, catching it early turns\\na user-reported quality incident into a quiet, pre-emptive fix.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## The `stopReason` field values\\nThe Converse API defines nine values ([Converse](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_Converse.html)). In invocation logs the field sits under `output.outputBodyJson.stopReason`, not at the top level of the record ([model invocation logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-invocation-logging.html)); native `InvokeModel` bodies use each provider\\'s own field.\\n| Value | Meaning |\\n|---|---|\\n| `end_turn` | Natural completion \u2014 the model finished its answer on its own. The healthy majority case. |\\n| `max_tokens` | **Truncation** \u2014 the model hit the output token limit and was cut off. The value to watch. |\\n| `stop_sequence` | The model emitted a configured stop sequence and halted (usually expected). |\\n| `tool_use` | The model paused to invoke a tool (agentic / tool-calling flows). |\\n| `guardrail_intervened` | A guardrail blocked or altered the response before completion. |\\n| `content_filtered` | The response was stopped by content filtering. |\\n| `malformed_model_output` | The model produced output that could not be parsed. |\\n| `malformed_tool_use` | The model produced a tool-use request that could not be parsed. |\\n| `model_context_window_exceeded` | **Truncation by context** \u2014 input plus output reached the model\\'s context window. Read it with `max_tokens`: a rise here is the \"prompts grew\" cause below. |\\n\\nA stable workload is dominated by `end_turn` (plus `tool_use` for agentic flows). A rising\\n`max_tokens` share is the regression indicator.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## What a shift from `end_turn` toward `max_tokens` means\\n\\nA growing `max_tokens` share means outputs are being cut off. The three usual causes:\\n\\n1. **Prompts grew.** A prompt-template change, a larger retrieved-context window, or longer\\n   conversation history crowds the output budget \u2014 the input eats into the room left for the\\n   response, so more answers hit the ceiling.\\n2. **`maxTokens` was reduced.** A configuration or deployment change lowered the output cap, so\\n   responses that used to complete now truncate.\\n3. **A model version changed generation length.** A new model/version generates longer answers for\\n   the same prompt and bumps into the existing cap.\\n\\nIn every case the shift **precedes visible quality complaints by hours or days** \u2014 users notice\\ntruncated answers only after the drift is well underway. When the shift correlates with a known\\ndeployment, treat the deployment as the prime suspect: roll back or adjust the output budget.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How to measure it\\n\\n**Prerequisite: model invocation logging must be enabled** (otherwise `stopReason` is never\\nemitted \u2014 this is a Bedrock invocation-logging area check). Without\\nit, LLM-EVAL-013 fires: the signal is simply invisible.\\n\\nOnce logging is on:\\n\\n1. Create a CloudWatch Logs **metric filter** on the Bedrock invocation log group:\\n   ```\\n   { $.output.outputBodyJson.stopReason = \"max_tokens\" }\\n   ```\\n   A filter on the top-level `$.stopReason` matches nothing, because the field is nested under\\n   `output.outputBodyJson`. Report such a filter under LLM-EVAL-013 as present but never matching.\\n2. Publish it as a **custom metric** (for example namespace `OpsAI/FinishReason/MaxTokens` with a\\n   `ModelId` dimension).\\n3. **Alarm** when the 1-hour `max_tokens` rate exceeds the established baseline by **more than 10\\n   percentage points**.\\n\\n> The **>10pp threshold is DERIVED, not AWS-published.** AWS documents the `stopReason` field and the\\n> metric-filter mechanism, but not a numeric drift bar. Treat 10pp as a sensible starting default and\\n> tune it per workload; report it as a derived/`workload-specific` value, never as an AWS number.\\n\\n### Logs Insights query \u2014 compute the distribution\\n\\nTo see the full distribution (not just the `max_tokens` count), run this CloudWatch Logs Insights\\nquery over the invocation log group:\\n\\n```\\nfields @timestamp, modelId, output.outputBodyJson.stopReason as stopReason\\n| filter ispresent(output.outputBodyJson.stopReason)\\n| stats count(*) as invocations by stopReason, modelId\\n| sort invocations desc\\n```\\n\\nCompare the `max_tokens` share across two windows (baseline vs current) to quantify the shift.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Correlated signals\\n\\nA finish-reason drift rarely travels alone. Corroborate it with:\\n\\n- **`OutputTokenCount` spikes** \u2014 responses getting longer is often the leading edge of a truncation\\n  shift (and always raises cost). This is check **LLM-EVAL-014**.\\n- **`InvocationLatency` rising** \u2014 longer generations take longer, so latency often creeps up\\n  alongside the drift.\\n- **User complaints about truncated / cut-off answers** \u2014 the lagging, human-visible symptom the\\n  distribution shift precedes.\\n\\nIf the `max_tokens` share is climbing *and* `OutputTokenCount` is climbing *and* a prompt or model\\nchange landed in the same window, the diagnosis is strong: outputs grew, the output budget is being\\nexhausted, and quality is regressing through truncation.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Linked checks\\n\\n| check-id | Family | What it covers |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| LLM-EVAL-012 | Evaluation | The finish-reason distribution **shift itself** \u2014 the regression signal. |\\n| LLM-EVAL-013 | Evaluation | **No metric filter** on `stopReason`, so the shift cannot be trended. |\\n| LLM-EVAL-014 | Evaluation | **`OutputTokenCount` rising** with flat `Invocations` \u2014 the correlated precursor. |\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_Eg6l9CuIdq4GJ2K3brO36O", "content": "[{'text': '# Metrics & Logs Reference \u2014 evaluation and quality signals\\n\\nHow to **collect** the quality signals this skill reasons about. The analysis of what a\\nfinish-reason shift means lives in `references/finish-reason-analysis.md`; this file is the\\ncollection mechanics \u2014 which log group, which field, which query, which metric.\\n\\nTrimmed deliberately to the evaluation set. Guardrail, agent, SageMaker endpoint, cost and triage\\nmetrics are **not** this skill\\'s scope: a finding built on them fails the scope rule. SageMaker-side\\nevaluation job signals are in scope and are in \u00a77.\\n\\nAll metric names are as published by AWS. Thresholds are never invented here \u2014 the only\\nnumeric bar in this domain is the **derived** >10pp finish-reason bar recorded in\\n`references/finish-reason-analysis.md`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. The invocation log group \u2014 resolve it, never assume it\\n\\n`stopReason` is **not** a CloudWatch metric. There is no `AWS/Bedrock` metric for finish\\nreasons, so the only honest route to a measured finish-reason distribution is a query against\\nthe Bedrock **model invocation logs**.\\n\\n**Always probe the logging configuration first.** The log group name is a customer choice and\\ndiffers per account:\\n\\n```\\nbedrock:GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration     (read-only, no arguments)\\n```\\n\\nRead three fields from the response:\\n\\n| Field | Why it decides the answer |\\n|---|---|\\n| `cloudWatchConfig.logGroupName` | the group to query; absent \u2192 CloudWatch delivery is off |\\n| `textDataDeliveryEnabled` | `false` \u2192 records arrive without prompt/response text |\\n| `s3Config.bucketName` | S3-only delivery \u2192 query with Athena, not Logs Insights |\\n\\nThen branch, and say which branch you took:\\n\\n- **Logging enabled** \u2192 query the named group (below) and report the distribution with\\n  **both** the current and the baseline share (LLM-EVAL-012).\\n- **Enabled but the query is denied or returns nothing in the window** \u2192 name the group, say\\n  the query was attempted, say what came back, and say the consequence. That is an honest\\n  answer and a complete one.\\n- **Logging disabled** \u2192 state that finish-reason drift **cannot be confirmed** from metrics\\n  alone, name what would be needed (invocation logging with text delivery, or the\\n  LLM-EVAL-013 metric filter), and claim **no measurement**. The signal is each response's finish reason (`stopReason`). Responses that end in `max_tokens` were cut off at the output limit. Responses that end in `end_turn` finished on their own. The finish reason isn't a CloudWatch metric, so the default Bedrock dashboards won't show it.

**1. Check that invocation logging is on.**
- Call `bedrock:GetModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration` to get the log group name. Don't assume the name.
- If CloudWatch delivery is off, you can't confirm the drift from metrics alone. Turn logging on first, with text delivery enabled.
- If delivery is S3-only, run the same query in Athena instead of Logs Insights.

**2. Compare two time windows.** Run this Logs Insights query over the last few days. Then run it again over an earlier window of the same length:

```
fields @timestamp, modelId, output.outputBodyJson.stopReason as stopReason
| filter ispresent(stopReason)
| stats count(*) as calls by stopReason, modelId
| sort calls desc
```

- Convert the counts to the `max_tokens` share per model for each window. A single number doesn't show a trend.
- The share should be mostly `end_turn`, plus `tool_use` if you use tools or agents. A rising `max_tokens` share confirms the cut-offs.
- Also watch `model_context_window_exceeded`. It means the input and output together hit the context limit, which is a different kind of truncation.
- Error records have no finish reason, so the `ispresent` filter drops them from the totals.
- Spot-check one raw record first. Some model families put the field on a different path, such as `stop_reason`.

**3. Look at related signals.** These help explain the cause but don't prove truncation by themselves.
- In the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace, `OutputTokenCount` rising while `Invocations` stays flat suggests responses are getting longer.
- `InvocationLatency` creeping up points the same way.
- `input.inputTokenCount` in the logs shows whether your prompts have grown.

**4. Find the cause.** If `max_tokens` is rising, it's usually one of three things:
- Prompts grew, for example from a template change, more retrieved context, or longer chat history.
- Someone lowered `maxTokens`.
- A model version change made answers longer.

Compare the date the shift began against your deployments and config changes before you raise the cap.

**5. Set up monitoring so you see it earlier next time.**
- Create a metric filter on the invocation log group with the pattern `{ $.output.outputBodyJson.stopReason = "max_tokens" }`. A filter on top-level `$.stopReason` never matches.
- Alarm when the hourly `max_tokens` rate is more than about 10 percentage points above your baseline. That 10-point figure is my suggested starting default, not an AWS number, so tune it to your workload.

This only works for Bedrock-hosted models. On a SageMaker endpoint or a self-hosted model, the finish-reason logs aren't available this way.
